## Summary of what I found (all machine-checked unless marked otherwise)

### 1. The project is double-counting: 17056 is 1112 in disguise

**Claim (proved, exact polynomial identity, checked with sympy):**
R(17056)(x, y) = R(1112)(xy, x/y). The exponent map (a,b) ↦ (a+b, a−b) has determinant −2, so for every odd m it permutes the characters (j,k) ↦ (j+k, j−k) of (Z/m)² bijectively. Hence 1112 and 17056 have *identical eigenvalue multisets at every odd m*, and identical periods. 17056 is confined at 37 because 1112 is; it carries no independent evidence. I searched all pairs of the 16 for exponent-map equivalence mod 37 (any L ∈ GL₂(Z/37), via basis-image matching) and mod 61: this is the only pair. So the "16 unexplained" are 15, and the "2,112 invertible exponent maps" check should have caught this.

### 2. The chance model is wrong for two of the classes, by a factor of ~3 each

For the square family, **f(x,1) and f(x,x) are one-dimensional rule-90 polynomials**: O(a,b)(x,1) = 0 for 0<b<a and for a=b>0, O(a,0)(x,1) = t(x^a), and O(a,b)(x,x) = 0 unless a=b, with O(a,a)(x,x) = t(x^{2a}) = t(x^a)². So the eigenvalues in the classes (0,1) and (1,1) are Q(θ) with θ = ζ+ζ⁻¹ and Q ∈ GF(2)[T] of degree ≤ 4 — only 32 possible values each.

**Computed (m = 37):** 30 of these 32 values are cubes or zero; the only non-cubes are Q = 1+t(x)+t(x⁴) and 1+t(x²)+t(x³)+t(x⁴). Over the whole family the per-class cube fractions at 37 are: (0,1): 0.937, (1,1): 0.937, (1,6): 1 (forced into F(2⁹)), the other eight classes 0.33–0.39. The chance model's "1/3 per free class" is therefore off by ~8× per rule. Using the empirical marginals under independence, the family-wide expectation is ≈ 5.7 all-cube rules (I counted 110 all-cube rules in the family at 37 in total; the project's 34 "beyond mechanisms 1–4" is consistent with that). The residual 15 (not 16) against ≈ 5–6 expected is a ~2.5× excess, p ≈ 10⁻³ — real, but far from "16 against 0.62". I do not know *why* 30/32 small Q(θ) are cubes at 37; it is a one-dimensional fact about rule 90 at 37 and should be investigated in the 1-D family first (conjecture: it is tied to rule 90's own cube confinement at 37; at m = 61, where rule 90 is not confined, the count is 17/32, only a mild bias).

### 3. Every confined rule is a cube in the group algebra — and for 9 of the 16 the cube root is anomalously sparse

The group algebra A = GF(2)[(Z/37)²] is semisimple (37 odd), A ≅ ⊕ over Frobenius-classes of fields. So **f has all nonzero eigenvalues cubes ⇔ f ≡ g³ mod (x³⁷−1, y³⁷−1) for some g ∈ A**, and g can be taken symmetric (proved: choose cube roots class by class; on the class (1,6), whose stabiliser acts as the 2⁹-Frobenius, the eigenvalue is in F(2⁹) where cubing is bijective, so the root is unique and compatible). This is a tautology, so a "mechanism" can only mean a *small* g. There are 3^k cube roots (k = free classes). I computed all of them for all 16 rules and recorded the minimum support size, runner-up, and median (median ≈ 650 of 1369 points, as for a random symmetric element):

| rule | min wt | next | | rule | min wt | next |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10498 | **172** | 444 | | 22064 | 428 | 452 |
| 1112, 17056 | **192** | 400 | | 4850 | 440 | 452 |
| 18246 | **224** | 400 | | 5972 | 448 | 472 |
| 2436 | **228** | 436 | | 28586 | 452 | 464 |
| 3461 | **249** | 425 | | 25183 | 453 | 461 |
| 26883 | **249** | 425 | | 13822 | 468 | 476 |
| 13584 | **268** | 452 | | 27390 | 476 | 484 |
| 28944 | **228** | 444 | | | | |

The minimum of ~20,000–60,000 roughly-binomial weights would be expected around 450–500, as in the right-hand group. The nine rules on the left have *one* cube root far below that, separated from the runner-up by a gap of 150–270 points. This is the signal of a real mechanism; the seven on the right look like chance (consistent with the corrected expectation of ≈ 5–6 chance confinements in §2). **The three rules confined at 61 (3461, 18246, 26883) all lie in the structured group**, which is what one would expect if the structure is real and the seven are noise.

I verified g³ ≡ f in the group algebra for all 16 minimal roots; for 1112, 10498, 2436 the sparse root is written out as a union of orbits in the JSON below (28, 24 and 31 orbits). I did **not** find a closed form for these g (no exponent-map image of them lands in a small box with entries ≤ 4; they are not dilation-invariant). Finding what these sparse g's are — e.g. whether g = (small unit)·(product of t(x^a y^b)-type factors) — is the concrete next step; the chance of a 172-point root arising from a 3¹⁰ search by accident is negligible.

### 4. At m = 61

Computed: 3461 has all 17 nonzero classes cubes; the class (1,11) (11² ≡ −1, 2¹⁵ ≡ 11) is forced into F(2¹⁵) ⊂ cubes, the other 16 are free and lie in F(2³⁰) proper, so no subfield/norm mechanism applies. Chance for one rule is 0.53² · 3⁻¹⁴ ≈ 6·10⁻⁸; three in the family is not chance. I could not finish the 3¹⁶ cube-root profile at 61 within my compute budget; **prediction to register:** each of 3461, 18246, 26883 has a cube root mod (x⁶¹−1, y⁶¹−1) whose support is below 40% of the median root weight, with a gap of >100 points to the runner-up, while a random confined rule would not.

### 5. Where I think the project is wrong or missing something
- The headline "16 vs 0.62" is wrong on both sides: 16 → 15 (§1), 0.62 → ≈5–6 (§2). The genuinely anomalous set is the 9 (really 8 up to equivalence) with sparse cube roots.
- The two-variable factorisation question can be bypassed entirely: work in the semisimple group algebra, where cube roots are explicit and finitely many; "has a mechanism" should be operationalised as "has a sparse or structured cube root", which is checkable.
- The one-dimensional fact (30/32 small Q(θ) cubes at 37) is unexplained and feeds every 2-D count; it should be proved or refuted on its own.

## Summary of what I found (all machine-checked unless marked otherwise)

### 1. The project is double-counting: 17056 is 1112 in disguise

**Claim (proved, exact polynomial identity, checked with sympy):**
R(17056)(x, y) = R(1112)(xy, x/y). The exponent map (a,b) ↦ (a+b, a−b) has determinant −2, so for every odd m it permutes the characters (j,k) ↦ (j+k, j−k) of (Z/m)² bijectively. Hence 1112 and 17056 have *identical eigenvalue multisets at every odd m*, and identical periods. 17056 is confined at 37 because 1112 is; it carries no independent evidence. I searched all pairs of the 16 for exponent-map equivalence mod 37 (any L ∈ GL₂(Z/37), via basis-image matching) and mod 61: this is the only pair. So the "16 unexplained" are 15, and the "2,112 invertible exponent maps" check should have caught this.

### 2. The chance model is wrong for two of the classes, by a factor of ~3 each

For the square family, **f(x,1) and f(x,x) are one-dimensional rule-90 polynomials**: O(a,b)(x,1) = 0 for 0<b<a and for a=b>0, O(a,0)(x,1) = t(x^a), and O(a,b)(x,x) = 0 unless a=b, with O(a,a)(x,x) = t(x^{2a}) = t(x^a)². So the eigenvalues in the classes (0,1) and (1,1) are Q(θ) with θ = ζ+ζ⁻¹ and Q ∈ GF(2)[T] of degree ≤ 4 — only 32 possible values each.

**Computed (m = 37):** 30 of these 32 values are cubes or zero; the only non-cubes are Q = 1+t(x)+t(x⁴) and 1+t(x²)+t(x³)+t(x⁴). Over the whole family the per-class cube fractions at 37 are: (0,1): 0.937, (1,1): 0.937, (1,6): 1 (forced into F(2⁹)), the other eight classes 0.33–0.39. The chance model's "1/3 per free class" is therefore off by ~8× per rule. Using the empirical marginals under independence, the family-wide expectation is ≈ 5.7 all-cube rules (I counted 110 all-cube rules in the family at 37 in total; the project's 34 "beyond mechanisms 1–4" is consistent with that). The residual 15 (not 16) against ≈ 5–6 expected is a ~2.5× excess, p ≈ 10⁻³ — real, but far from "16 against 0.62". I do not know *why* 30/32 small Q(θ) are cubes at 37; it is a one-dimensional fact about rule 90 at 37 and should be investigated in the 1-D family first (conjecture: it is tied to rule 90's own cube confinement at 37; at m = 61, where rule 90 is not confined, the count is 17/32, only a mild bias).

### 3. Every confined rule is a cube in the group algebra — and for 9 of the 16 the cube root is anomalously sparse

The group algebra A = GF(2)[(Z/37)²] is semisimple (37 odd), A ≅ ⊕ over Frobenius-classes of fields. So **f has all nonzero eigenvalues cubes ⇔ f ≡ g³ mod (x³⁷−1, y³⁷−1) for some g ∈ A**, and g can be taken symmetric (proved: choose cube roots class by class; on the class (1,6), whose stabiliser acts as the 2⁹-Frobenius, the eigenvalue is in F(2⁹) where cubing is bijective, so the root is unique and compatible).
